findings.title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, blocking team admins
findings.body: The permission check computes `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, requiring the caller to be BOTH an admin and an owner. A user who is a team admin but not the owner is denied, even though the variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and the intent is clearly OR. Team admins (who are not owners) will incorrectly receive FORBIDDEN when adding guests to team bookings. Fix to `||`.

findings.title: Email comparisons are case-sensitive, allowing blacklist bypass and duplicates
findings.body: The blacklist is lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`) but the guest emails from input are not, and `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` compares exactly. A guest email like `User@Example.com` bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries and can duplicate an existing attendee record (Prisma will happily create a second attendee row differing only in case), which also breaks the later `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` matching in sendAddGuestsEmails. Emails should be normalized (trim + lowercase) before all comparisons.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the original `guests` array rather than `uniqueGuests` (the emails actually added after filtering out existing attendees and blacklisted addresses). Consequently, an attendee whose email was already on the booking (i.e., not newly added) matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and receives an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a full 'you are scheduled' email with callToAction) instead of the 'guests added' notification, and blacklisted/filtered emails still influence email routing. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the calling user's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, ... })` use the session user, who per the permission check may be merely an attendee of the booking. The EventManager then calls `updateCalendarAttendees`, which tries to update the event on the organizer's connected calendar using the attendee's credentials. For an attendee caller this will fail or use the wrong integration, and even when the caller is the organizer but a team booking, the booking's actual host credentials (already fetched via `booking.user.credentials` include) are ignored. The event manager should be built from the booking organizer (`booking.user`), not `ctx.user`.

findings.title: No guard against cancelled bookings or seat-capacity overflow
findings.body: The handler adds guests without checking `booking.status` or `booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot`. Guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings (sending 'guests added' emails and calendar updates for an event that no longer exists), and for seat-based event types the attendee count can be pushed past `seatsPerTimeSlot`, corrupting the seat invariant. Validate the booking is in an active state and, for seated event types, that adding the guests does not exceed capacity.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event type metadata
findings.body: Every other send*Emails function in this file accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host/attendee emails when `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` is set (e.g., workflows-managed event types). `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata parameter and the handler in addGuests.handler.ts never passes it, so hosts/attendees who explicitly disabled standard emails will still receive these emails. The function should honor the same suppression flags, and eventType metadata should be passed from the handler.

findings.title: Subject name uses attendees[0].name which may be an empty-name new guest
findings.body: The organizer email subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. The addGuests handler creates attendee rows with `name: ""` for new guests, and the attendee ordering is not guaranteed, so the organizer's subject can render as 'Guests Added: 30min with  at ...' (empty name) or crash if attendees is empty. Prefer the original booker's name (the attendee who created the booking) or fall back to email.

findings.title: Error path swallows the error object with a bare console.log
findings.body: The catch around `sendAddGuestsEmails` only logs the literal string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and discards `err`, so email delivery failures are undiagnosable in production. Log the error (ideally via the structured logger used elsewhere) so failures can be debugged.

findings.title: Validation error banner never clears once shown
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true when validation fails but is only reset on Cancel. If the user corrects the emails and clicks Add again, the mutation runs while the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner stays visible, and if the mutation succeeds the toast plus stale error banner give contradictory feedback. Reset `isInvalidEmail` (or clear it when validation succeeds) before/inside handleAdd.

findings.title: Guests array has no max length limit
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` is unbounded, so a caller can submit thousands of emails in one request. The handler then creates that many attendee rows in a single `createMany`, sends that many emails, and issues a large calendar update — an easy amplification/DoS vector for any authenticated user. Add a `.max(...)` (consistent with other booking endpoints) or enforce a limit in the handler.
